title: Stateful TTL reconciliation and phased rollback safeguards for VPC operator upgrades
creator: Ava Martin
description: Critical work to prevent on-prem/VPC operator upgrade failures caused by stateful CR reconciliation during Helm lifecycle events. Introduce a safe-upgrade mode, phased rollback policy, and TTL-aware reconciliation backoff to reduce config-drift and customer escalations.
background: Over the last two months we've seen multiple customer escalations where Helm-driven upgrades to the VPC/on-prem operator triggered aggressive reconciliation loops that left stateful resources (node agents, persistent workloads) transiently orphaned or GC'd. Symptoms included degraded control-plane responsiveness, Helm releases stuck in post-upgrade hooks, and customers forced into manual rollbacks. Existing fixes addressed immediate incidents but did not prevent race conditions between leader election, CR ownerRef mutation, and post-upgrade hooks.
impact_summary: This fixes a high-severity escalation vector affecting Dedicated and Private deployments during operator upgrades. Customers run risk of downtime, manual intervention, and data-plane instability. The mitigation will reduce customer interruptions and operator upgrade blast radius.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy operator v2.8.5 with stateful CRs (nodeagent, storage-driver) in a VPC cluster
2) Trigger Helm upgrade to operator-2.9.0 with post-upgrade hooks enabled
3) Simulate brief control-plane leader swap (kill leader pod) during hook execution
4) Observe CR controller requeue storms, ownerRef mutation, and Helm release stuck in post-upgrade hook (kubectl describe release shows hanging hook pod).
5) Recreate at scale to trigger resource churn and API throttling.
investigation_summary: Investigation (logs, heap profiles, API server traces) showed a narrow timing window: Helm post-upgrade hooks executed a mutation that removed a controller-managed ownerRef for stateful CRs while leader election was reassigning pods. The operator reconciler immediately retried and attempted resource recreation/GC. Under load this produced reconciliation storms and API throttling. We also found missed leader-health gating in our Helm pre-upgrade checks.
root_cause: Race between Helm post-upgrade resource mutations and operator reconciliation + missing 'safe-upgrade' coordination. OwnerRef mutation and TTL annotations caused operator to treat resources as drifted and attempt destructive reconciliation while cluster leadership was unstable.
proposed_solution: 1) Add operator 'safe-upgrade' feature flag that temporarily disables destructive reconciliation for listed CR kinds during upgrades. 2) Implement TTL-aware reconciliation backoff: reconcile backoff increases if a CR was recently mutated by a Helm hook. 3) Add a phased rollout + automated canary check in Helm charts (pre-upgrade drain + leader-check). 4) Ship a customer-facing rollback runbook and an automated ownerRef repair job for affected clusters.
decision: Approve implementation of safe-upgrade feature (operator-2.9.0) and require Helm release templates to include pre-upgrade leader health check hook. Do not attempt an in-place forced GC removal in the hotfix; instead provide a repair job and a staged rollout path for customers.
implementation_notes: - Operator: introduce --safe-upgrade flag and annotation 'redwood.io/safe-upgrade: v2'
- Reconciler: implement recent-mutation cache (5m window) and exponentially increasing backoff for CRs with helm-hook annotation
- Helm: add pre-upgrade hook that verifies leader endpoint and blocks if leader flip detected
- Runbook: automated ownerRef repair job as a Job/DaemonSet that can be applied by customers

Initial rollout as staged canary to 5 internal customers, monitor metrics for 72 hours, then broad roll-out.
